topStories.headline: Alice Griffith Housing Crisis Deepens as Pelosi, Advocates Demand Accountability
topStories.dek: Bayview's flagship affordable housing complex faces mounting scrutiny over rodent infestations, habitability violations, and mass debt notices sent to tenants.
topStories.body:
Residents of Alice Griffith Apartments in Bayview–Hunters Point are living amid a documented rodent infestation and accumulating code violations that have drawn the attention of federal elected officials and state investigators. Mission Local reported in late July 2026 that tenants continue to encounter rats despite assurances from property management that the problem had been addressed. One resident told the outlet she was startled by a rodent as recently as July 20, and Mission Local reporters who visited the property on July 21 observed debris in piles in the trash room and an intense smell emanating from the first floor.

The apartment complex, developed as the flagship success story of the Candlestick Point / Hunters Point Shipyard Phase 2 redevelopment, has been cited for numerous health code violations, some of which have never been addressed. On July 14, 2026, tenants received mass 'Balance Due' notices, prompting advocates at Destination Freedom Media Group to call for an independent audit of management's financial records and a moratorium on eviction filings until habitability obligations are verified.

Nancy Pelosi, who once championed the construction of Alice Griffith Apartments, called tenants' allegations 'deeply concerning,' according to Mission Local's July 23, 2026 report. Tenants have previously delivered direct testimony to a Special Assistant Attorney General at the California Department of Justice, describing mold, broken elevators, sewage backups, and a reported cluster of approximately ten deaths at the complex since January 2026.

The San Francisco Housing Authority has documented more than 129 deficiencies at the property in a single year, according to the Davis Vanguard's ongoing investigative series. The John Stewart Company manages the property; the company has not responded publicly to the specific allegations reported this week. City officials have faced growing pressure to act, with advocates noting that no contract suspensions or large-scale enforcement actions have been publicly announced against the operators.

topStories.headline: Muni Adds Frequency on Key Routes Starting August 29, Including 8AX Benefiting Visitacion Valley Students
topStories.dek: SFMTA's latest round of systemwide service improvements coincides with the start of the SFUSD school year and eliminates a transfer requirement for Visitacion Valley riders.
topStories.body:
The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency announced this week a series of systemwide Muni improvements set to begin Saturday, August 29, 2026. The changes are designed to reduce crowding during peak commute hours and improve reliability across some of the city's busiest routes, at no additional cost to the agency.

Among the changes most relevant to the Bayview and Excelsior cluster: students traveling from Visitacion Valley to Francisco Middle School on the 8AX-Bayshore Express will no longer need a transfer pass under the new schedule. The adjustments are timed to align with the start of the San Francisco Unified School District school year on August 17.

Systemwide highlights include the N-Judah improving from every 10 minutes to every nine minutes during peak hours — a change SFMTA Director of Transportation Julie Kirschbaum said would bring immediate improvements to thousands of riders. The 5R-Fulton Rapid will return to 60-foot buses every 10 minutes, restoring capacity that was reduced in February when the Potrero bus facility closed. Morning peak-hour capacity is also being expanded on the 22-Fillmore, 29-Sunset, 38R-Geary Rapid, and 49-Van Ness/Mission lines.

The SFMTA said the changes are cost-neutral, citing approximately $250 million in identified operational efficiency savings across the system. The agency said the improvements were informed by rider feedback, operator input, and service data from earlier adjustments that took effect in June.

topStories.headline: Black-Owned Bookstore and Café Chapter 3 Coming to Bayview's Third Street
topStories.dek: Smoke Soul Kitchen owner Vanessa Lee has filed permits to open a bookstore and café at 4512 Third Street, which would be the first general bookstore in Bayview–Hunters Point in years.
topStories.body:
Vanessa Lee, the owner of Smoke Soul Kitchen on Third Street in Bayview–Hunters Point, has filed a permit application to open a new Black-owned bookstore and café called Chapter 3 at 4512 Third St., between La Salle Avenue and Third Street, Mission Local and Shelf Awareness reported in July 2026. Lee told Mission Local she plans to open the establishment by the end of this year.

Chapter 3 would fill a former MetroPCS storefront and become the first general-interest bookstore in the neighborhood since Just A Touch Christian Bookstore closed more than two years ago. Lee said she was inspired by Marcus Books, the historic Black-owned bookstore that once operated in the Fillmore before relocating to Oakland, and described her vision as a gathering place the community deserves.

The café component will serve brunch on weekends and transition to a wine bar in the evenings. Lee also plans to host author readings and live performances. Chapter 3 is one of nine Bayview businesses awarded Storefront Opportunity Grants this year from the city's Office of Economic and Workforce Development — a program designed to help fill vacant storefronts on the Third Street corridor, which has faced persistent vacancies since the pandemic. Gumbo Social, also on Third Street, separately announced this week a crowdfunding campaign to launch a pilot evening takeout window open from 6 PM to 10 PM, citing the neighborhood's limited after-dark dining options.

moreNews.headline: Gumbo Social Launches Crowdfund to Open Evening Takeout Window on Third Street
moreNews.body: Bayview's beloved Gumbo Social, which currently closes at 6 PM, announced on July 28, 2026 a crowdfunding campaign to launch a pilot evening takeout window open from 6 PM to 10 PM at 5176 Third Street. Owner Dontaye Ball said the walk-up window would address the neighborhood's limited after-dark dining options and could encourage other Third Street businesses to extend their hours. The restaurant noted it is temporarily closed through August 16 but remains open for catering and at Café Mélange inside SF City Hall.

moreNews.headline: Mission: Comics and Arts to Open Second Location in the Excelsior
moreNews.body: Mission: Comics and Arts, which has operated out of 2250 Mission St. since 2008, is opening a second location in the Excelsior District with the help of a $50,000 grant from the San Francisco Office of Economic and Workforce Development's storefront vacancy program, Mission Local reported in May 2026. Owner Leef Smith, who grew up in the Excelsior, said the shop may be the first comics store ever to open in the neighborhood. The OEWD grant will help cover upfront plumbing and electrical costs in the older commercial building.

moreNews.headline: Hunters Point Shipyard Contamination: Parcel C Cleanup on Track for Late 2026
moreNews.body: The U.S. Navy's final phase of cleanup at Parcel C of the Hunters Point Naval Shipyard — the 78-acre tract where airborne plutonium-239 was detected at above-action levels in November 2024, a finding not disclosed to the city for 11 months — is scheduled for completion in fall 2026, according to reporting by Mission Local. The Navy apologized to the San Francisco Board of Supervisors in December 2025 for the delayed disclosure. Additional radiological material was discovered in a cabinet inside a secure building at the shipyard in April 2026, with the Navy stating the find was unrelated to the active cleanup project. Community advocates and District 10 Supervisor Shamann Walton have continued to press for greater transparency.
